LESSON: WRITING 8.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.4: Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing, part of Strand 8 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do you enjoy listening to and reading stories? 2. How do you make a story interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. organise thoughts fluently, clearly and precisely in a coherent paragraph for self- expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create a narrative composition of about 60- 80 words for self- expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. promote the role of creativity in writing for different purposes.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing,

   Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. organise thoughts fluently, clearly and precisely in a coherent paragraph for self- expression,

   Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. create a narrative composition of about 60- 80 words for self- expression,

   Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. promote the role of creativity in writing for different purposes.

   Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. re-arrange jumbled up sentences from an oral narrative into a coherent paragraph,

2. listen to a narrative on radio and rewrite it in their own words,

3. plan a narrative composition collaboratively,

4. use similes to make the narrative interesting,

5. write a narrative composition for self-expression,

6. watch and dramatise a story from a digital device,

7. visit a farm and write a narrative composition about their experience. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. re-arrange jumbled up sentences from an oral narrative into a coherent paragraph,
2. listen to a narrative on radio and rewrite it in their own words,
3. plan a narrative composition collaboratively,
4. use similes to make the narrative interesting,
5. write a narrative composition for self-expression,
6. watch and dramatise a story from a digital device,
7. visit a farm and write a narrative composition about their experience. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration. This is enhanced as the learner plans a narrative composition with peers.

● Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner creates, watches and dramatises a narrative composition.

64

Value:

Responsibility: It is nurtured as the learner observes safety precautions as they visit a farm and write a narrative composition

about their experience.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental Education: This is enhanced as the learner learns about crops and animals found in the farm as well as

their welfare.

• Social Cohesion: This inculcated as the learner interacts with peers while performing activities like visiting the farm with

peers.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of writing a narrative composition for self-expression to composition writing in Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing,
2. organise thoughts fluently, clearly and precisely in a coherent paragraph for self- expression,
3. create a narrative composition of about 60- 80 words for self- expression,
4. promote the role of creativity in writing for different purposes.

Remember the key question: Why do you enjoy listening to and reading stories? 2. How do you make a story interesting?
